findings.highlight: Blood drips down my fingers where they grasp the knife
findings.evidenceJa: ナイフを握った指に血が滲む
findings.governingReading: Blood seeps into or wells on the fingers gripping the knife.
findings.explanation: The English changes gradual seepage at the grip into blood running downward.

findings.highlight: the sob rising in my throat
findings.evidenceJa: 胸の奥からせりあがってきた嗚咽
findings.governingReading: A sob rises from deep in Shirou’s chest.
findings.explanation: The English relocates the sob’s origin to his throat.

findings.highlight: My eyes are hot
findings.evidenceJa: 目蓋が熱い
findings.governingReading: Shirou’s eyelids feel hot with restrained tears.
findings.explanation: The English changes the eyelids to the eyes themselves.

findings.highlight: My path was set
findings.evidenceJa: 致命的なまでに、この答えは決まっていた
findings.governingReading: The answer had been fixed to a fatal or decisive degree since he embraced Sakura in the rain.
findings.explanation: The English removes the fatal severity and turns the answer into a generalized path.

findings.highlight: [blank page]
findings.evidenceJa: 裏切るのか
findings.governingReading: The inward accusing voice asks, “Will you betray it?”
findings.explanation: mirror moon leaves the entire hinge accusation blank.

findings.highlight: My body is wracked by contradictory thoughts
findings.evidenceJa: 相反する思考が体をズタズタに切り崩していく
findings.governingReading: The conflicting thoughts cut and tear Shirou’s body to pieces.
findings.explanation: The English keeps distress but removes the progressive bodily dismemberment image.

findings.highlight: A selfish superhero
findings.evidenceJa: もとから身勝手にすぎない正義の味方
findings.governingReading: The accusing voice calls him an ally of justice who was nothing but selfish from the beginning.
findings.explanation: The English removes both the retrospective scope and the absolute degree.

findings.highlight: Kiritsugu threw away his own wishes
findings.evidenceJa: 私情を切り捨てた切嗣
findings.governingReading: Kiritsugu cut away private feelings for the sake of what he believed.
findings.explanation: The English changes personal attachments and feelings into wishes.

findings.highlight: helps others just because of self-interest
findings.evidenceJa: 私情だけで誰かを助ける無力な人間
findings.governingReading: The counterimage is a powerless human who saves someone from private feeling alone.
findings.explanation: The English gives the motive the more selfish and calculating coloration of self-interest.

findings.highlight: The idea I believed in for ten years
findings.evidenceJa: 十年間信じ続けてきた[ruby text=おもい char=2]自分
findings.governingReading: The surface “self” is read as “feeling/thought,” binding Shirou’s decade-long ideal to his identity.
findings.explanation: The English turns the layered self into a detached idea.

findings.highlight: is piercing my heart
findings.evidenceJa: 立ち止まる自分の胸を打つ
findings.governingReading: The decade-long self or ideal strikes the chest of the present self who has stopped.
findings.explanation: The English loses the confrontation between two selves and changes striking the chest into piercing the heart.

findings.highlight: Will I betray myself, who cried and tried to live on, ignoring the voices of the people who died helplessly?
findings.evidenceJa: 目の前で成す術もなく死んでいった人々の声を、涙しながら、ただ一人生き延びようとした自分を裏切るのか
findings.governingReading: The accusation asks whether Shirou will betray the voices of those who died helplessly before him and the weeping self who alone tried to survive.
findings.explanation: The English collapses the two objects of betrayal and invents that Shirou ignored the dead people’s voices.

findings.highlight: who had to cling to that atonement
findings.evidenceJa: 死んでいった彼らに報いなければ
findings.governingReading: Shirou clung to the feeling that he could not live unless he repaid those who died.
findings.explanation: The English removes the dead as the recipients and object of the atonement.

findings.highlight: I can’t make amends for this crime
findings.evidenceJa: 取り繕って無視できる罪でもない
findings.governingReading: The sin cannot be patched over with appearances and ignored.
findings.explanation: The English replaces impossible evasion with inability to make amends.

findings.highlight: after losing what I’ve believed in until now
findings.evidenceJa: 今まで信じ、支えてきたモノをなくして
findings.governingReading: Shirou loses what he has believed in and what has sustained him until now.
findings.explanation: The English removes the ideal’s role in sustaining him.

findings.highlight: I will betray them
findings.evidenceJa: 裏切るとも
findings.governingReading: Shirou emphatically accepts betraying the sustaining self or ideal under accusation.
findings.explanation: The English pluralizes the referent into an unspecified “them.”

findings.highlight: If Sakura’s smile is there, I won’t even care
findings.evidenceJa: 桜の笑顔があるのならそれでいい
findings.governingReading: If Sakura’s smile is there, that alone is enough for Shirou despite living by self-deception.
findings.explanation: The English changes tragic sufficiency into indifference to the moral cost.

findings.highlight: There’s nothing wrong with it
findings.evidenceJa: この思いに間違いはない
findings.governingReading: Shirou says there is no mistake in this feeling or desire.
findings.explanation: The English turns subjective certainty into a broader declaration that the choice is morally unobjectionable.

findings.highlight: I need Sakura. Sakura needs me
findings.evidenceJa: 桜を必要とした自分。桜が必要とした自分
findings.governingReading: Shirou identifies the self who needed Sakura and the self whom Sakura needed in a balanced pair.
findings.explanation: The English preserves reciprocal need but removes the identity-focused parallel construction.

findings.highlight: right when I’m about to…
findings.evidenceJa: ナイフを戻そうとした瞬間
findings.governingReading: Sakura speaks at the exact moment Shirou is about to return or withdraw the knife.
findings.explanation: The English suppresses the action behind an ellipsis, weakening proof that he had abandoned the strike before she spoke.

findings.highlight: It’s not sadness about having me kill her. She’s apologizing for making me resort to this
findings.evidenceJa: 俺が桜を殺しにきた事ではなく。そうさせてしまった事を謝罪するような
findings.governingReading: Sakura’s expression seems to apologize not for Shirou having come to kill her, but for having driven him to do so.
findings.explanation: The English invents sadness, shifts “came to kill” into Sakura having him kill her, and weakens the distinction between act and cause.

findings.highlight: She’s apologizing
findings.evidenceJa: 涙する寸前の顔
findings.governingReading: Sakura’s face is on the verge of tears.
findings.explanation: The English omits the visible extremity of her expression.

findings.highlight: I hear fear in Sakura’s voice
findings.evidenceJa: 本気で言っているのか
findings.governingReading: Shirou inwardly asks whether Sakura truly means what she said.
findings.explanation: The English omits his disbelief and immediately substitutes an emotional observation.

findings.highlight: I hear fear in Sakura’s voice
findings.evidenceJa: 桜の声には懇願と、隠しようのない怯えがある
findings.governingReading: Sakura’s voice contains both a plea and fear she cannot conceal.
findings.explanation: The English removes the plea and the impossibility of concealing her fear.

findings.highlight: I was so preoccupied that I didn’t even notice it?
findings.evidenceJa: こんな事に気付かないほど、俺は追い詰められていたのか
findings.governingReading: Shirou realizes he was driven so far into a corner that he failed to notice Sakura’s state.
findings.explanation: The English reduces acute psychological entrapment to distraction.

findings.highlight: Sakura’s determination
findings.evidenceJa: 眠ったふりをして俺を生かそうとした桜の覚悟
findings.governingReading: Sakura’s resolve consisted in pretending to sleep so that Shirou would live.
findings.explanation: The English removes the entire action, motive, and life-or-death protective reversal.

findings.highlight: what tomorrow is
findings.evidenceJa: 明日は何があるのか
findings.governingReading: Sakura can no longer tell what will happen tomorrow.
findings.explanation: The English changes future events into the malformed abstraction “what tomorrow is.”

findings.highlight: asked for help
findings.evidenceJa: ずっと助けてって言っていた
findings.governingReading: Sakura says she had kept asking for help all along.
findings.explanation: The English removes the duration and persistence of her pleas.

findings.highlight: I ignored everything, thinking it’s just a dream
findings.evidenceJa: この夢はただの夢だって見て見ぬフリをしてきました
findings.governingReading: Sakura treated the dream as merely a dream and deliberately pretended not to see it.
findings.explanation: The English generalizes the object to everything and loses the willful seeing-without-acknowledging mechanism.

findings.highlight: all I could do was curse them
findings.evidenceJa: 恨む事しかできなくて
findings.governingReading: Sakura condemns herself as capable only of resenting others.
findings.explanation: The English changes sustained resentment into actively cursing them.

findings.highlight: me, the one who watches it
findings.evidenceJa: あんな夢を見るわたし自身
findings.governingReading: Sakura condemns the self who has such dreams.
findings.explanation: The English separates her from the dream by making her its watcher rather than dreamer.

findings.highlight: forget about you
findings.evidenceJa: 先輩のコトもわからなくなる
findings.governingReading: Sakura fears she will cease to recognize or understand Shirou.
findings.explanation: The English changes loss of recognition into forgetting about him.

findings.highlight: before I become the bad guy
findings.evidenceJa: わたしが悪い自分になる前に
findings.governingReading: Sakura asks to be stopped before she becomes a bad version of herself.
findings.explanation: The English replaces her split self-conception with the generic role of “the bad guy.”

findings.highlight: If you can finish it here
findings.evidenceJa: 先輩の手で終わらせてもらえるなら
findings.governingReading: Sakura asks to have Shirou end her life by his own hand.
findings.explanation: The English leaves the object of “finish it” unspecified and omits his hand as the means.

findings.highlight: with all my strength
findings.evidenceJa: 背中を掻き毟るように、ありったけの力で
findings.governingReading: Shirou receives and holds Sakura with all his strength, as though clawing at her back.
findings.explanation: The English retains maximum strength but removes the desperate clawing image.

findings.highlight: She’s scared of dying
findings.evidenceJa: 死ぬのが怖いクセに、死にたくないクセに
findings.governingReading: Sakura is both afraid of death and does not want to die, despite asking to be killed.
findings.explanation: The English omits her explicit desire to live.

findings.highlight: It’s too late
findings.evidenceJa: そんなのもうしてる
findings.governingReading: Shirou answers that he is already regretting it.
findings.explanation: The English changes an ongoing emotion into a generic claim that the opportunity has passed.

findings.highlight: A quiet sobbing
findings.evidenceJa: 静かな嗚咽
findings.governingReading: A quiet sob is heard during the embrace.
findings.explanation: The English renders the noun phrase ungrammatically.

findings.highlight: I promise Sakura as she cries
findings.evidenceJa: 涙する桜に声をかける
findings.governingReading: Still embracing, Shirou speaks to the crying Sakura.
findings.explanation: The English labels the speech act as a promise rather than preserving the neutral act of addressing her.

findings.highlight: I swore to be Sakura’s superhero
findings.evidenceJa: 桜の味方をすると誓った
findings.governingReading: Shirou swore that night to be Sakura’s ally or take her side.
findings.explanation: The English turns the route-defining rejection of the ally-of-justice role into becoming Sakura’s superhero.
